reasoning_traces.think:
The watch–remember–reason framework formalizes human video comprehension as a sequential cognitive pipeline. Watch maps raw video inputs to structured visual tokens E(t) via spatiotemporal encoding. Remember preserves these tokens in a memory state M(t) using either short-term (STM) or long-term (LTM) mechanisms. Reason then infers grounded outcomes P(t) by combining E(t), M(t), and prior knowledge. This triadic structure enables modular extension: e.g., memory can be replaced with graph-based storage, or reasoning can be augmented with external knowledge bases. Failure modes include loss of temporal coherence in E(t), forgetting in M(t), and misalignment in R(P|·). Dualities emerge in how STM vs. LTM encode information, and how agent-based vs. deterministic memory systems interact with reasoning modules. The framework supports scalable architectures by decoupling functional components while maintaining causal fidelity.
